reason: The liver-cell picture shows glucose entering from blood and being joined into a stored carbohydrate.
expectation: The liver cells will turn some of the absorbed glucose into a store.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the digestive organs is the other goal, but I will make the glucose store first.

effect: The glucose is now stored as linked carbohydrate inside liver cells; connecting the digestive organs remains.
reaction: It is useful to see that the store can be broken down again between meals.
reason: The remaining goal is to connect the digestive organs to the body, so these two pieces are the obvious match.
expectation: The digestive tract will connect to the body's circulation and other systems.

effect: The digestive tract is connected to circulation, completing the chapter; the colon's inner wall remains unassembled.
reaction: The connection makes sense, though the unfinished colon opening makes me curious about what comes next.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the liver carbohydrate store was most worthwhile: it showed how some glucose can be saved and later broken down for fuel.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the digestive tract was straightforward but less engaging because the goal already named the connection.

surprise.text: I hadn't expected the completed body picture to leave the colon's inner wall unassembled.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary: the liver-cell picture showed glucose storage, and the other pairing matched the connection goal.

continue.text: I would choose to continue to see how the colon's inner wall fits into the digestive system, although this chapter's two pairings were fairly predictable.
